report:
### Conclusion
The claim is **strongly supported by clinical evidence**. Subcutaneous abaloparatide substantially reduces the risk of new vertebral fractures in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis.

### Evidence in Favor
* **Phase III ACTIVE Trial**: In the landmark 18-month randomized clinical trial, postmenopausal women receiving abaloparatide experienced an **86% relative risk reduction** in new morphometric vertebral fractures compared to placebo (0.58% vs. 4.22%, $P < 0.001$), alongside significant increases in bone mineral density (BMD) (https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2544640).
* **Systematic Reviews**: Systematic reviews and meta-analyses confirm that abaloparatide consistently provides robust vertebral fracture prevention and BMD improvement across postmenopausal study populations (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38307725/).

### Limitations and Safety Considerations
Despite high efficacy, treatment involves notable clinical trade-offs and usage bounds:
* **Adverse Reactions**: Common side effects include dizziness, nausea, palpitations, hypercalcemia, hypercalciuria, and transient orthostatic hypotension (https://www.dovepress.com/abaloparatide-and-the-spine-a-narrative-review-peer-reviewed-fulltext-article-CIA).
* **Treatment Duration & Warnings**: Prescribing guidelines note a boxed warning regarding osteosarcoma risk (based on rodent studies), limiting cumulative lifetime exposure to anabolic agents like abaloparatide to two years (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2017/208743lbl.pdf).

### Sources
* JAMA: https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2544640
* PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38307725/
* FDA Label: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2017/208743lbl.pdf
* Clinical Interventions in Aging: https://www.dovepress.com/abaloparatide-and-the-spine-a-narrative-review-peer-reviewed-fulltext-article-CIA
